observation_summary: The Closure Compiler incorrectly reports a type mismatch error when a function returns an object that is constructed conditionally across multiple branches, failing to correctly merge the types of the object properties.
reasoning_summary: The issue is a failure in the type-checking algorithm's ability to correctly infer and merge the union of object types across conditional branches. This is a procedural logic error in how the compiler's type-checking engine processes object property assignments within control flow, rather than a missing guard (Checking), a wrong constant (Assignment), or a design-level capability gap (Function/Class/Object).
evidence_used: assignment to object in conditional causes type error on function w/ record type return type
evidence_gaps: The specific internal type-merging logic code is not provided, only the test case and the resulting error.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The error is not caused by a missing guard or validation check, but by an incorrect inference of the resulting type after merging branches.
The capability to check types exists; the algorithm for merging them is simply flawed in this specific scenario.
